tasks.title: Complete UI for Workspaces Management
tasks.description: Develop a comprehensive user interface for managing workspaces, including creation, editing, deletion, and navigation between different workspace environments.
tasks.details:
Implement a full-featured workspace management interface that includes:

1. **Workspace Dashboard**: Create a main dashboard displaying all available workspaces with visual cards showing workspace name, description, last modified date, and member count.

2. **Workspace Creation Flow**: Build a multi-step form for creating new workspaces with fields for name, description, privacy settings (public/private), and initial member invitations. Include validation for required fields and duplicate workspace names.

3. **Workspace Settings Panel**: Develop a comprehensive settings interface allowing workspace owners to:
   - Edit workspace metadata (name, description, icon)
   - Manage member permissions and roles
   - Configure workspace-specific settings
   - Archive or delete workspaces with confirmation dialogs

4. **Navigation Components**: Implement workspace switcher dropdown in the main navigation, breadcrumb navigation showing current workspace context, and quick access sidebar for recently used workspaces.

5. **Member Management Interface**: Create UI components for inviting new members, displaying current members with their roles, and managing member permissions with role-based access controls.

6. **Responsive Design**: Ensure all workspace management interfaces work seamlessly across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices with appropriate touch interactions and responsive layouts.

7. **Loading States and Error Handling**: Implement proper loading indicators for async operations, error messages for failed actions, and empty states when no workspaces exist.

Technical considerations:
- Use modern CSS Grid/Flexbox for layouts
- Implement proper form validation with real-time feedback
- Include accessibility features (ARIA labels, keyboard navigation)
- Optimize for performance with lazy loading of workspace data
- Follow established design system patterns and components
tasks.testStrategy:
Verification approach:

1. **Functional Testing**: Test all CRUD operations (create, read, update, delete) for workspaces through the UI. Verify workspace creation with various input combinations, editing of existing workspaces, and proper deletion with confirmation flows.

2. **User Experience Testing**: Navigate through the complete workspace management flow from dashboard to creation to settings. Test workspace switching functionality and verify proper context updates throughout the application.

3. **Form Validation Testing**: Submit forms with invalid data (empty required fields, duplicate names, invalid characters) and verify appropriate error messages display. Test real-time validation feedback during user input.

4. **Responsive Design Testing**: Test all workspace management interfaces on different screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop) and verify proper layout adaptation, touch interactions, and accessibility features.

5. **Member Management Testing**: Test member invitation flow, role assignment changes, and permission updates. Verify proper display of member lists and accurate role-based UI restrictions.

6. **Error Handling Testing**: Simulate network failures, server errors, and edge cases to verify proper error message display and graceful degradation of functionality.

7. **Performance Testing**: Verify loading times for workspace lists, smooth transitions between views, and proper loading state indicators during async operations.

8. **Cross-browser Testing**: Test functionality across major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) to ensure consistent behavior and appearance.

9. **Accessibility Testing**: Use screen readers and keyboard-only navigation to verify all workspace management features are accessible to users with disabilities.

tasks.title: Implement Dynamic Workspace Functionality
tasks.description: Add backend functionality and API endpoints to make workspaces fully operational with dynamic data management, real-time updates, and user interactions.
tasks.details:
Implement the core backend functionality to support dynamic workspace operations:

1. **Database Schema & Models**: Create comprehensive database models for workspaces including tables for workspace metadata, user-workspace relationships, permissions, and activity logs. Implement proper indexing for performance optimization.

2. **API Endpoints**: Develop RESTful API endpoints for all workspace operations:
   - GET /api/workspaces - List user's workspaces with pagination
   - POST /api/workspaces - Create new workspace
   - PUT /api/workspaces/:id - Update workspace details
   - DELETE /api/workspaces/:id - Delete workspace (with cascade handling)
   - GET /api/workspaces/:id/members - Manage workspace membership
   - POST /api/workspaces/:id/invite - Send workspace invitations

3. **Real-time Updates**: Implement WebSocket connections or Server-Sent Events for live workspace updates, member activity notifications, and collaborative features.

4. **Permission System**: Build role-based access control (RBAC) with roles like Owner, Admin, Member, and Viewer. Implement middleware for route protection and permission validation.

5. **Data Validation & Security**: Add comprehensive input validation, sanitization, and security measures including rate limiting, CSRF protection, and proper error handling.

6. **Caching Layer**: Implement Redis or similar caching for frequently accessed workspace data to improve performance.

7. **Integration Points**: Connect the backend APIs with the existing UI components, ensuring proper error handling and loading states.
tasks.testStrategy:
Comprehensive testing approach:

1. **API Testing**: Use tools like Postman or automated test suites to verify all endpoints work correctly with various input scenarios, including edge cases and error conditions. Test authentication and authorization for each endpoint.

2. **Database Testing**: Verify data integrity, proper relationships, and cascade operations. Test with large datasets to ensure performance meets requirements.

3. **Real-time Functionality**: Test WebSocket connections with multiple concurrent users, verify message delivery, and test connection recovery scenarios.

4. **Permission Testing**: Thoroughly test role-based access control by attempting operations with different user roles and verifying proper access restrictions.

5. **Integration Testing**: Test the complete flow from UI interactions through API calls to database operations, ensuring data consistency and proper error propagation.

6. **Performance Testing**: Load test the APIs with concurrent requests, measure response times, and verify caching effectiveness.

7. **Security Testing**: Perform security audits including SQL injection tests, XSS prevention verification, and authentication bypass attempts.

tasks.title: Implement Dynamic Notifications System
tasks.description: Build a comprehensive notifications system with real-time delivery, user preferences, and dynamic content based on workspace activities and user interactions.
tasks.details:
Implement a full-featured notifications system that provides real-time updates and user engagement:

1. **Backend Notification Service**: Create a notification service with database models for notifications including notification types (workspace invites, activity updates, mentions, deadlines), recipient targeting, read/unread status, and timestamps. Implement notification templates for different event types and user roles.

2. **Real-time Delivery System**: Integrate WebSocket connections or Server-Sent Events (SSE) to push notifications instantly to connected users. Implement fallback mechanisms for offline users including email notifications and in-app notification queuing.

3. **Notification API Endpoints**: Develop RESTful endpoints for notification management:
   - GET /api/notifications - Fetch user notifications with pagination and filtering
   - PUT /api/notifications/:id/read - Mark notifications as read
   - POST /api/notifications/preferences - Update user notification preferences
   - DELETE /api/notifications/:id - Delete specific notifications

4. **Frontend Notification Components**: Build React components for notification display including a notification bell icon with unread count, dropdown notification list, notification cards with action buttons, and a comprehensive notification center page.

5. **User Preferences System**: Implement notification settings allowing users to control notification types (email, in-app, push), frequency settings, and workspace-specific preferences. Include options for quiet hours and notification grouping.

6. **Event Triggers Integration**: Connect the notification system to workspace events such as new member additions, task assignments, file uploads, comments, and workspace updates. Implement intelligent notification batching to prevent spam.
tasks.testStrategy:
Comprehensive testing strategy for notification functionality:

1. **Real-time Testing**: Verify WebSocket/SSE connections work correctly across different browsers and network conditions. Test notification delivery speed and reliability, including connection recovery after network interruptions.

2. **API Endpoint Testing**: Use automated tests to verify all notification endpoints handle various scenarios including bulk operations, permission checks, and error conditions. Test pagination and filtering functionality with large notification datasets.

3. **User Interface Testing**: Test notification components across different screen sizes and devices. Verify notification bell updates correctly, dropdown displays properly, and notification center loads efficiently with proper infinite scrolling.

4. **Integration Testing**: Verify notifications are triggered correctly by workspace events. Test notification preferences are respected and different notification types are delivered through appropriate channels (in-app, email).

5. **Performance Testing**: Test system performance with high notification volumes and multiple concurrent users. Verify notification queuing works properly for offline users and batch processing doesn't create delays.

6. **Cross-browser Testing**: Ensure notification features work consistently across Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge, including permission handling for browser notifications.

tasks.title: Standardize Details Page Sections and Cards
tasks.description: Create a unified design system and component library for all sections and cards displayed on details pages across the application to ensure consistent user experience and maintainable code.
tasks.details:
Implement a comprehensive standardization of details page components to create visual and functional consistency:

1. **Component Audit and Analysis**: Conduct a thorough review of all existing details pages (workspace details, user profiles, project details, etc.) to identify current card/section patterns, inconsistencies in styling, spacing, typography, and interaction behaviors. Document all variations and create a standardization plan.

2. **Design System Components**: Create reusable React components for standardized sections including:
   - `DetailCard` component with consistent padding, borders, shadows, and hover states
   - `SectionHeader` with standardized typography, spacing, and optional action buttons
   - `InfoSection` for displaying key-value pairs with consistent formatting
   - `ActionSection` for buttons and interactive elements with unified styling
   - `StatusBadge` components for displaying various states (active, pending, archived)

3. **CSS/SCSS Standardization**: Establish consistent design tokens including:
   - Standardized spacing units (8px grid system)
   - Consistent color palette for backgrounds, borders, and text
   - Typography scale with defined font sizes, weights, and line heights
   - Shadow and border-radius standards for depth and visual hierarchy
   - Responsive breakpoints for mobile and desktop layouts

4. **Layout Grid System**: Implement a flexible grid system for details pages that adapts to different content types while maintaining visual consistency. Define standard layouts for single-column, two-column, and three-column arrangements.

5. **Component Migration**: Systematically replace existing ad-hoc sections with standardized components across all details pages, ensuring backward compatibility and maintaining existing functionality while improving visual consistency.
tasks.testStrategy:
Comprehensive testing approach to ensure standardization quality and consistency:

1. **Visual Regression Testing**: Use tools like Percy, Chromatic, or manual screenshot comparison to verify that all details pages maintain consistent visual appearance across different screen sizes and browsers. Test each standardized component in isolation and within page contexts.

2. **Component Library Testing**: Create Storybook stories or similar documentation for each standardized component, testing all possible states, props combinations, and edge cases. Verify components render correctly with various content lengths and data types.

3. **Cross-Page Consistency Audit**: Manually review all details pages (workspace details, user profiles, project pages) to ensure consistent spacing, typography, colors, and interaction patterns. Create a checklist of standardization criteria and verify each page meets all requirements.

4. **Responsive Design Testing**: Test all standardized components and pages across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports to ensure consistent behavior and appearance. Verify that grid systems and spacing adapt appropriately to different screen sizes.

5. **Accessibility Testing**: Verify that standardized components meet WCAG guidelines including proper color contrast ratios, keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, and focus management. Test with accessibility tools like axe-core or Lighthouse.

6. **Performance Impact Assessment**: Measure page load times and bundle sizes before and after standardization to ensure the new components don't negatively impact performance. Verify that CSS is optimized and unused styles are eliminated.

subtasks.description: Review all existing details pages to identify current card and section patterns, inconsistencies in styling, spacing, typography, and interaction behaviors. Document all variations and create a plan for standardization.
subtasks.details: Analyze workspace details, user profiles, project details, and other relevant pages. Record findings in a shared document for reference in subsequent tasks.

subtasks.title: Define and Design Standardized Components
subtasks.description: Design reusable React components for standardized sections and cards, including DetailCard, SectionHeader, InfoSection, ActionSection, and StatusBadge, ensuring consistent UI and interaction patterns.
subtasks.details: Create component specifications and design mockups based on audit findings. Ensure each component adheres to the Single Responsibility Principle and avoids duplication.

subtasks.title: Establish CSS/SCSS Design Tokens and Standards
subtasks.description: Develop a set of design tokens for spacing, color palette, typography, shadows, border-radius, and responsive breakpoints to ensure visual consistency across all components.
subtasks.details: Document and implement standardized variables and mixins in the CSS/SCSS codebase. Align tokens with the design system and component requirements.

subtasks.title: Implement Layout Grid System
subtasks.description: Create a flexible grid system for details pages that supports single-column, two-column, and three-column layouts while maintaining visual consistency.
subtasks.details: Define grid breakpoints and layout rules. Integrate the grid system with standardized components for seamless page composition.

subtasks.title: Migrate Existing Components to Standardized System

subtasks.details: Plan and execute migration in phases, starting with high-traffic pages. Monitor for regressions and coordinate with QA for validation.

subtasks.title: Set Up Documentation and Storybook
subtasks.description: Document all standardized components, design tokens, and layout systems. Create Storybook stories for each component to facilitate developer onboarding and usage.
subtasks.details: Write clear usage guidelines, code examples, and visual references. Ensure documentation is accessible and kept up to date.

subtasks.title: Perform Regression and Accessibility Testing
subtasks.description: Conduct comprehensive visual regression and accessibility testing on all standardized details pages to ensure consistency, usability, and compliance with accessibility standards.
subtasks.details: Use automated tools and manual review to verify visual consistency, keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility, and color contrast. Address any issues found.

tasks.title: Implement Skeleton Loading Components for Details Pages
tasks.description: Create skeleton loading components that mirror the structure and layout of standardized details page sections and cards to provide smooth loading states and improved user experience.
tasks.details:
Implement comprehensive skeleton loading components based on the standardized details page structure:

1. **Skeleton Component Architecture**: Create a flexible skeleton system with base skeleton components (SkeletonCard, SkeletonSection, SkeletonText, SkeletonAvatar, SkeletonButton) that can be composed to match the exact layout of standardized details page sections. Implement props for customizing dimensions, animation speed, and shape variations.

2. **Details Page Skeleton Mapping**: For each standardized details page section/card type, create corresponding skeleton components that match the exact layout structure:
   - WorkspaceDetailsSkeleton: Mirror workspace info cards, member lists, activity feeds
   - UserProfileSkeleton: Match profile header, stats cards, recent activity sections
   - ProjectDetailsSkeleton: Replicate project info, timeline, team member cards
   - Ensure skeleton dimensions and spacing exactly match the loaded content

3. **Animation and Visual Polish**: Implement smooth shimmer animations using CSS keyframes or libraries like react-loading-skeleton. Add subtle pulse effects and gradient animations that feel natural and indicate loading progress. Ensure animations are performant and don't cause layout shifts.

4. **Responsive Skeleton Behavior**: Make skeleton components responsive to match the responsive behavior of actual content. Implement breakpoint-specific skeleton layouts that adapt to different screen sizes, ensuring consistency between skeleton and loaded states.

5. **Integration with Loading States**: Create hooks or utilities (useSkeletonState, withSkeleton HOC) to seamlessly integrate skeleton components with data fetching states. Implement automatic skeleton display during initial loads, refetching, and error recovery scenarios.

6. **Accessibility Considerations**: Add proper ARIA labels, screen reader announcements for loading states, and ensure skeleton components don't interfere with keyboard navigation or assistive technologies.
tasks.testStrategy:
Comprehensive testing approach for skeleton loading functionality:

1. **Visual Consistency Testing**: Compare skeleton components side-by-side with actual loaded content to verify exact layout matching. Test across different screen sizes and devices to ensure responsive skeleton behavior matches responsive content behavior. Use visual regression testing tools to catch any layout discrepancies.

2. **Loading State Integration Testing**: Test skeleton display during various loading scenarios including initial page loads, data refetching, slow network conditions, and error recovery. Verify smooth transitions between skeleton and loaded content without layout shifts or visual glitches.

3. **Performance Testing**: Measure skeleton animation performance across different devices and browsers. Ensure animations don't cause frame drops or excessive CPU usage. Test skeleton rendering speed compared to empty states or loading spinners.

4. **Accessibility Testing**: Verify skeleton components work correctly with screen readers and provide appropriate loading announcements. Test keyboard navigation isn't blocked by skeleton states. Ensure proper ARIA labels and roles are implemented.

5. **Cross-browser Compatibility**: Test skeleton animations and layouts across major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) to ensure consistent appearance and behavior. Verify CSS animations work correctly in all target browsers.

6. **User Experience Testing**: Conduct user testing to verify skeleton loading feels natural and improves perceived performance. Test with real network conditions and various content loading speeds to ensure skeleton timing feels appropriate.

subtasks.title: Design and Implement Base Skeleton Component Architecture
subtasks.description: Develop a flexible skeleton system with reusable base components (SkeletonCard, SkeletonSection, SkeletonText, SkeletonAvatar, SkeletonButton). Ensure these components support props for customizing dimensions, animation speed, and shape variations to match the standardized details page layout.
subtasks.details: Establish a component architecture that allows for easy composition and customization. Implement core animation (shimmer, pulse) and ensure visual consistency across all skeleton elements.

subtasks.title: Map and Build Skeleton Variants for Standardized Details Pages
subtasks.description: Create skeleton components that mirror the structure of each standardized details page section and card type, such as WorkspaceDetailsSkeleton, UserProfileSkeleton, and ProjectDetailsSkeleton. Ensure these variants match the exact layout, dimensions, and spacing of their loaded counterparts.
subtasks.details: For each details page type, analyze the layout and build corresponding skeleton variants using the base components. Validate that skeletons are visually identical to the loaded state and adapt responsively to different screen sizes.
